title: Modules courbes elliptiques en caractéristiques ≠2 : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: the notes on moduli of elliptic curves in characteristic ≠ 2 begin with a combinatorial section, '2. Structures de carré combinatoire'. The four objects in play (likely the four 2-torsion or branch points) carry a 'square' structure, with automorphism group D_4, a Sylow 2-subgroup of S_4. This page finishes listing equivalent descriptions of a square structure and makes the passages between them explicit.

The five descriptions:
(1) An incidence system Q = (S, A, R): 4 vertices, 4 edges, incidence R ⊂ S×A.
(2) A 4-element set S with a fixed-point-free involution, equivalently a partition into two pairs. D = S/a is the set of diagonals.
(3) Dually, a 4-element set A with a partition into two pairs. C = A/a is the set of codiagonals, i.e. pairs of opposite edges.
(2 bis) S is a torsor under a group Γ that is a 'form' of Z/4Z: Γ is cyclic of order 4 with no chosen generator, and in a topos it is a twisted form classified by H^1(Aut Z/4 = Z/2).
(3 bis) A is a torsor under Γ.

Passages:
- 2bis → 2 and 3bis → 3: take the unique element a of order 2 in Γ. It acts as a fixed-point-free involution (the antipody), and D = S/a, resp. C = A/a.
- 2 → 1: put A = P_2(S) \ Im D. These are the 6 − 2 = 4 two-element subsets that are not diagonals, i.e. the edges. R ⊂ S×A is tautological membership.
- 3 → 1: put S = P_2(A) \ Im C. These are the 4 pairs of non-opposite (adjacent) edges, each identified with its common vertex. The tautological R' ⊂ A×S is transposed to give R.
- 1 → 2bis, 3bis: let 𝔇 = Aut Q, of order 8. It maps isomorphically onto Sylow 2-subgroups of 𝔊_S = Sym(S) and of 𝔊_A = Sym(A).
  - The inverse images in 𝔇 of the Klein subgroups V_S ⊂ 𝔊_S and V_A ⊂ 𝔊_A are two subgroups of order 4.
  - V_S consists of 1, a, and the two reflections whose axes pass through midpoints of opposite edges. These reflections are indexed by C, so V_S ≅ F_2^C canonically: a ↔ (1,1), elements of C ↔ the delta functions.
  - Dually, V_A ≅ F_2^D, the reflections in the diagonals.
  - The crossed-out lines, continued on the next page, show that the third order-4 subgroup is the unique cyclic one, 𝔇^+. Both S and A are torsors under 𝔇^+, which plays the role of Γ.

Conceptually, this is the equivalence of several groupoids, all equivalent to the classifying groupoid B(D_4). D_4 = Hol(Z/4Z) = Z/4 ⋊ Aut(Z/4) is exactly the automorphism group of a pair (Γ, Γ-torsor). This is the set-up for a later relation to D_4 ⊂ S_4, i.e. the choice of a pairing of the 4 points. For elliptic curves this is plausibly a Γ_0(2)-type level structure.
errors: No mathematical errors on this page. The counts (6 − 2 = 4) and both tautological constructions are correct.
The notation F_2^C ≅ V_S is correct and in fact canonical (a ↔ constant function 1), though it is not explained on the page.

Minor: in (2 bis)/(3 bis) the group must be allowed to vary as a form of Z/4Z, not be fixed. Otherwise the groupoid of torsors would have automorphism group Z/4 rather than D_4. Grothendieck's word 'forme' indicates he means this.
On the next page, 'D^+_ab ≅ D/{1,a}' is a slip for D_ab = D/{1,a}. 𝔇^+ is cyclic of order 4, so it is not of rank 2 over F_2.

ideas.what: Equivalent descriptions of a combinatorial square: incidence system, a 4-set with pairing (diagonals), dual 4-set with pairing (codiagonals), torsor under a twisted form of Z/4Z
ideas.modern_name: Equivalent groupoids all equivalent to BD_4; D_4 as holomorph of Z/4Z; flag/incidence description of the 4-gon
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (dihedral group combinatorics); the stack-theoretic viewpoint is standard folklore
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme discusses polygons/dessins and twisted forms in a related spirit, but not this specific list

ideas.what: Reconstructing edges as non-diagonal 2-subsets of vertices and vertices as non-opposite pairs of edges
ideas.modern_name: Duality of the square (4-cycle graph self-duality)

ideas.what: D_4 = Aut(square) as a Sylow 2-subgroup of S_4, with its three index-2 subgroups V_S, V_A, 𝔇^+ (two Klein, one cyclic); canonical identifications V_S ≅ F_2^C, V_A ≅ F_2^D

deep.surprise_reason: This is careful but elementary bookkeeping: equivalent descriptions of a square structure and the structure of D_4 ⊂ S_4. It is typical of Grothendieck's style (twisted forms, torsors, canonical identifications) but contains nothing new to specialists. Its interest lies only as preparation for the level-structure combinatorics of elliptic curves later in the notes.
transcription_corrections: Line 3: 'par la donnée d'un groupe R' — the symbol is most likely Γ (a 'forme' de Z/4Z), consistent with 'torseur sous Γ' in the following lines.
The phrase 'ordre 8' is written under/near '𝔇 = Aut Q', i.e. 𝔇 has order 8. 'Q = {S, A, R}' is the incidence system.
The margin diagram reads F_2^C ≃ V_S ↪ 𝔊_S and F_2^D ≃ V_A ↪ 𝔊_A, with 𝔇 mapping to both 𝔊_S and 𝔊_A (the first arrow appears labelled with 𝔇_S).

'notés F_2^C ⊂ 𝔇 et V_A' — the order-4 subgroups are identified as F_2^C (= V_S) and F_2^D (= V_A). The struck-out continuation mentions the two elements of order 4, inverse to one another, which the next page resumes.
'Voici [?]' at the end of the explanatory paragraph is uncertain in the image.
